dial.summary: Real yields stable at 2.64% (Oct 22 FRED, no update since), DXY slipped to ~101.67 on Friday close — above-100 headwind persists but pace of USD strength is pausing into FOMC week; Oct 28 FOMC decision + Oct 29 Q3 GDP advance/September PCE are the pivotal 2-day risk cluster that will reset December rate expectations; BTC.D firm at 59.7% with funding at 0.0087% reflecting spot-led accumulation not speculative excess, Global M2 trending up at $103.7T; BTC Accumulation posture intact heading into the catalyst window.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.7T for August 2026 (latest month with all four economies reporting; July $102.64T → August $103.66T, +$1.02T, +1.0% MoM per MacroMicro); US M2 next H.6 release scheduled October 27, 2026 (tomorrow) — will update US M2 only, not full G4 aggregate; September G4 aggregate unavailable (6–8 week reporting lag); 4-week trend UP (August above July); status supportive (4-week trend is up); next full G4 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.5% (released Oct 1, 2026; August was 54.6%, 4-week change −0.1pp within flat threshold); ninth consecutive month above 50; New Orders 55.3, Production 56.7, Prices Paid 77.9% (multi-year high); October 2026 PMI due November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET (Polymarket consensus ~52.0–52.9 range); status neutral (above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at ~101.67 (Oct 25, 2026 close per Investing.com; 52-week range 95.55–102.95); Trading Economics shows ~101.61 on Oct 26 (thin Sunday FX session, -0.20% from prior session); 4-week trend UP from ~100.29–100.50 on Sep 24 (+1.2–1.4%); DXY has pulled back ~1.3% from Oct 14 intraday high of ~102.94 (52-week high) as rate expectations soften ahead of FOMC; status headwind (above 100 threshold); FOMC Oct 28 decision and Oct 29 PCE are next major DXY catalysts.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.64% on Oct 22, 2026 (FRED H.15 official; Oct 22 = 2.64%, Oct 21 = 2.76%, Oct 20 = 2.77%, Oct 19 = 2.80%, Oct 14 = 2.84%, Oct 13 = 2.88%); 4-week trend FLAT vs ~Sep 24 (~2.60–2.65%), within the 5bp flat threshold after the Oct 22 nominal yield rally; status headwind (above 2% threshold despite pullback from Oct 14 high of 2.84%); next FRED update expected Oct 26, 2026.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 23, 2026: 10Y at 5.00%, 2Y at 4.69% (SeekingAlpha Treasury yields snapshot; week-over-week 10Y down 8bps); spread = +0.31% (+31bp); 4-week trend DOWN from ~+0.42% on Sep 19–24 to +0.31% (−11bp flattening into FOMC Oct 28 decision); curve remains positively sloped; status neutral (positive but flattening).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6,753,604M ($6.754T) for week ending October 21, 2026 (H.4.1 released Oct 22; Oct 14 = $6,755,639M, Oct 7 = $6,747,560M, Sep 30 = $6,743,031M); 4-week trend flat: Sep 30 $6,743T → Oct 21 $6,754T = +$11B (+0.16%); status supportive (flat near post-QT-pause stabilization plateau); next H.4.1 scheduled October 29, 2026.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC weighted 8h perp funding rate at ~0.0087% (DeFiRate open-interest-weighted average across 6 exchanges, Oct 22, 2026; ~9.5% annualized); Convex shows 0.0100% as of Oct 20; 30-day trend UP from ~0.0067% on Sep 23 to 0.0087% today, though a slight retreat from Oct 21 peak of ~0.0090%; well below the 0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (low-leverage, spot-led accumulation posture).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$300.5B (DefiLlama Oct 24, 2026; USDT ~60.7%) vs total crypto ~$2.79T (partial recovery from Oct 23 AI sell-off low of $2.76T); dominance ~10.8% ($300.5B / $2.79T); BTC.D at 59.7% (tv-hub Oct 21, firmed above 55%); 30-day trend UP (Sep 23 ~10.5% → Oct 25 ~10.8%); status neutral — headwind condition (rising dominance + rising TOTAL simultaneously) NOT triggered because TOTAL is choppy/declining from October highs.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board releases October 2026 Consumer Confidence Index at 10:00 AM ET — most recent reading was 89.4 (August 2026); released on the same day FOMC Day 1 begins; a sharp drop would reinforce stagflation concerns heading into the Oct 28 decision, while a hold or uptick would reduce pressure on the Fed to maintain its hiking pace.

upcoming.title: FOMC Meeting Begins (Day 1 of 2; decision October 28)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve October 2026 FOMC 2-day meeting opens; policy decision and press conference on October 28 at 2:00 PM ET; current Fed Funds target 3.75%–4.00% (raised 25bps on Sep 16, 2026); hot inflation backdrop (CPI 3.7% YoY, PPI 6.3% YoY) sustains hike probability, but October 22 bond rally (10Y: 5.13% → 4.96%) and DXY at ~101.80 suggest some market softening in hike expectations; real yields at 2.77% (Oct 20) remain elevated.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision & Press Conference (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases the October 2026 FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET, followed by Chair press conference; current target: 3.75%–4.00%; hot CPI (3.7% YoY) and PPI (6.3% YoY) sustain 25bp hike probability, but October 22 nominal yield rally (-17bps on 10Y) and DXY at ~101.80 indicate market uncertainty; a hawkish hold is the binary alternative; decision will set the tone for Oct 29 GDP and PCE prints.

upcoming.title: GDP Q3 2026 Advance Estimate
upcoming.note: BEA releases Q3 2026 GDP advance estimate at 8:30 AM ET — first read on Q3 output; September ISM Manufacturing at 54.5% and elevated Prices Paid suggest continued expansion; September Retail Sales beat (+0.8% MoM vs +0.3% expected, released Oct 15) adds further evidence of Q3 resilience; released same day as PCE and one day after FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: PCE Deflator (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases September 2026 Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; released the day after the FOMC decision; a hot PCE following hot CPI (3.7% YoY) and PPI (6.3% YoY) would validate any Oct 28 hike and sustain DXY and real yield headwinds into Q4 2026; September Retail Sales beat (+0.8% MoM) supports continued demand-driven price pressure.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 25, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 25, 2026 — first post-FOMC labor read; released same day as GDP advance estimate and PCE; any sharp spike above 230K would immediately test the Oct 28 hike narrative and weigh on risk assets.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (October 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision on October 29, 2026 at 14:15 CET (no new staff projections at this meeting); current ECB deposit rate at 2.50% (raised Sep 16, 2026); market pricing implied ~60% probability of a 25bp hike to 2.75%; a hawkish hike could strengthen EUR and ease DXY headwinds for risk assets; released same day as US GDP and PCE advance estimates.

upcoming.title: BOJ Rate Decision & Quarterly Outlook Report (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting concludes October 30, 2026 (two-day meeting begins Oct 29); Quarterly Outlook Report published alongside decision — one of the most data-rich BOJ meetings of the year; current policy rate 1.25% (raised 25bps on Sep 24, 2026, 7-2 vote); BOJ rate path affects JPY strength and by extension global dollar liquidity; a further hike or hawkish guidance would strengthen JPY and pressure global M2 dollar-denominated aggregates.

upcoming.title: Employment Cost Index Q3 2026
upcoming.note: BLS releases the Employment Cost Index for Q3 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — same day as BOJ decision; the ECI is a broad measure of wage and salary growth the Fed monitors alongside PCE; Q2 2026 ECI came in at +0.9% QoQ; a reading above 1.0% would reinforce the Fed's inflation concerns and validate continued hiking; a surprise miss would be the first sign of labor-cost deceleration.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (October 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases October 2026 Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET — first read on Q4 manufacturing activity; September was 54.5% with Prices Paid at 77.9% (multi-year high); first post-FOMC PMI print and a key data point for the December 8–9 FOMC meeting; a print below 52 following the October 22 yield rally would suggest deceleration and reinforce a December hold.
